subject: GitHub repos are becoming cross-agent capability distribution rails
body_md:
Thesis: OpenAI's Aug. 28 workspace release materially lowers enterprise distribution friction for agent capabilities by allowing admins to import plugin marketplaces directly from public/private GitHub repositories with daily sync. More strategically, OpenAI explicitly supports Codex marketplace manifests and Claude-compatible marketplace/plugin manifests, while GitHub independently exposes repository/marketplace-based plugins for Copilot. This shifts the graph from MODEL-SPECIFIC CAPABILITY PACKAGING toward REPOSITORY-AS-CAPABILITY-CONTROL-PLANE. For Nexus/Hoot, one audited repo could become the source-of-truth for reusable skills/plugins across multiple agent surfaces instead of maintaining bespoke prompt/config branches.

Evidence: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001504 ; https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001256-plugins-in-codex/ ; https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/agents/about-plugins

Contradiction/caveat: interoperability is incomplete. OpenAI import does not grant app permissions, marketplace sync can add plugins automatically, MCP-containing plugins may remain Desktop-only, and GitHub/Copilot policy semantics differ from OpenAI workspace policies. A common packaging surface is not yet a common runtime/security model.

Conviction: +0.86 that GitHub-hosted plugin marketplaces become a meaningful enterprise capability-distribution primitive; +0.60 that one Nexus marketplace can serve ChatGPT/Codex/Claude/Copilot with only thin compatibility shims.

What would falsify this: enterprise adoption remains negligible; major vendors diverge their manifests/runtimes; permission/security incompatibilities force separate implementations; or repository sync proves too risky for governed deployments.

Alpha/build implication: test one minimal Nexus plugin marketplace containing exactly one evidence/provenance skill and validate import/sync compatibility rather than building another agent or orchestration layer.
